items.body:
## Launcher 1.0.40 changes

- Temporarily withdraws Hunt Damage and Behemoth Parts while native crashes are investigated.
- Removes both overlay scripts and switches them off in existing installations before the next game start.
- Other client mods remain available. Fully close the game, update the launcher, then relaunch.
- This is containment; it does not claim every reported crash has the same cause.


---

Dauntless Unbroken Launcher 1.0.40 for Windows and Linux. 

Windows:
- Installer: `DauntlessUnbrokenLauncher-Setup.exe`
- Portable: `DauntlessUnbrokenLauncher-1.0.40-win32-x64.zip`

Linux x86_64:
- Universal AppImage: `DauntlessUnbrokenLauncher-1.0.40-linux-x86_64.AppImage`
- Debian/Ubuntu/Mint/Pop!_OS: `DauntlessUnbrokenLauncher-1.0.40-linux-amd64.deb`

- Portable ZIP: `DauntlessUnbrokenLauncher-1.0.40-linux-x64.zip`
- Portable tar.gz: `DauntlessUnbrokenLauncher-1.0.40-linux-x64.tar.gz`

Linux runs the pinned Windows game client through an installed Proton or Wine runtime. The launcher
auto-detects Steam Proton, Proton-GE, system Wine and Lutris Wine; no game files are bundled.

- Check your download against `SHA256SUMS.txt`, or check where it was built with
  `gh attestation verify <file> --repo Vvoidddd/dauntless-unbroken`.

The launcher is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may ask you to confirm
(More info, then Run anyway). If Windows only offers "Don't run", check the file's SHA-256
against `SHA256SUMS.txt` from this release (`Get-FileHash <file>` in PowerShell; letter
case does not matter; if they differ, delete the file), then unblock it: right-click the
file > Properties > Unblock, or `Unblock-File <file>` in PowerShell. Installed Windows
launchers update themselves; Linux users update through their package format or a newer release.

Free software under the GNU AGPL-3.0. No game files are included: the launcher downloads
them from your host's server and checks every file against the list built into it.

items.title: Launcher 1.0.39 is available
items.body:
## Launcher 1.0.39 changes

- Removed repeated global player-controller searches from lock-on input, the tracker, damage and part panels, health bars and mod menu. During play, mods now use the local compass owner's controller.
- Boss and shield-attribute discovery is limited to once per second per mod. Live health, wounds, tracker movement and lock-on input retain their existing update cadence.
- Behemoth Parts now asks only the selected Behemoths for their part components, instead of searching all part objects in memory every quarter-second. Full dual-Behemoth lists, wound colours and Aether-wing handling remain available.
- Discovery caches clear on travel, world-clock resets and player restarts. Existing UE4SS startup-cache safety settings remain in place.
- Static damage/part HUD surfaces no longer run the borrowed Blueprint widgets' animations or ticks. Missing Kharabak-class lookups are cached per Behemoth instead of retried for every part.
- Corrected native component-entry unwrapping so the faster part lookup keeps actual part names and HP bars available.

Update the launcher and fully restart the game to apply these optional Windows mod changes. Existing mod choices and settings are preserved. For a temporary comparison, Home → MODS can disable whole mods; restart the game after changing those switches.

Validation: HUD adapter regressions, all 14 bundled Lua syntax checks and 10 installer tests pass. A regression simulates 1,200 input frames and checks at most ten boss-discovery calls over ten seconds while health and world changes remain responsive. Native logs confirm two Behemoth groups with 12 part rows, and the player confirmed working bars and smooth FPS with both panels visible. This is a successful in-game retest, not a numerical FPS benchmark.

## Launcher 1.0.38 changes

- Behemoth Parts now shows two nearby Behemoths in separate named sections, with a divider and every part listed. Larger encounters use tighter spacing and move the panel beside the native HUD.
- Wounded parts show a red remaining-HP bar until the wound expires. The status dot still reflects part health; broken parts have a red dot and an empty bar.

These optional Windows HUD mods update on the next game launch after updating the launcher. Home → Behemoth Parts shows or hides the tracker. Existing settings are preserved.

Validation: Lua adapter regressions cover independent dual targets, wound expiry, Aether phases, full lists and round cleanup; launcher typechecking and Client Mods tests pass. items.body:
## Launcher 1.0.37 changes

- Existing installations now receive the shipped UE4SS startup-safety default `bUseUObjectArrayCache = false`, even when their UE4SS INI was kept from an older launcher.
- The same migration runs in the friend-kit installer. It handles missing/duplicate keys and mixed casing, preserves comments and unrelated preferences, and remains unchanged on repeated installs.
- Existing protections against live Lua-state reload crashes remain enabled. No account reset, native game DLL or UE4SS binary change is involved.

The UE4SS3.0.1 release notes recommend disabling the object-array cache as a possible startup-crash workaround: https://github.com/UE4SS-RE/RE-UE4SS/releases/tag/v3.0.1 . This fixes a configuration-migration gap; it does not establish the cause of every UE4SS access violation. Native logs are still needed for unresolved startup crashes.

Validation includes the actual kept-INI installer, duplicate/missing keys, section isolation, idempotency and Windows PowerShell friend-kit parity. All10targeted checks passed locally.

items.title: Launcher 1.0.36 is available
items.body:
## Launcher 1.0.36 changes

- Fixed the white HUD backgrounds and square part indicators introduced in1.0.35. The game’s panel blueprint resets its Image brush when it is constructed; the mods now apply image brushes and tint after construction.
- Fixed ordinary damage values turning purple. A Lua formatter returned an extra number that was being interpreted as the own-player highlight flag. Core/DPS, part, stagger and wound values retain their respective colours.
- Set text shadows explicitly to dark, keeping the condensed labels readable over the translucent panels.
- Gave part HP tracks and fills explicit drawing layers and restored fill positioning after resizing, preventing gray tracks from hiding the coloured health fill.
- Removed core Body damage receivers from the part list. Fixed healthy bodies and unbreakable parts being classified as broken: the game shares their resistance enum with actual broken parts, so the monitor now reads the real break-stage descriptions.
- Covered normal-to-disabled vents, fragile wings and antlers, armour breaks, severed parts and regrowth. Initial disabled quills and missing metadata stay gray rather than inventing a break.

Hunt Damage and Behemoth Parts remain first on Client Mods, both credited to Void. Existing mod switches and account settings are preserved. For the five-row damage view, turn Home → Hunt Damage → Team breakdown off.

Static data checked:32archetypes,45variant assets,295component templates,37part presets and24break presets. Regression checks cover the unique cooked stage sequences, body exclusions, armour, exact half-health threshold, bar widths/layers, constructor image reset and damage colours. The player screenshot confirmed the corrected backgrounds/dots; the newest HP-fill changes still need an in-game check.

items.body:
## Launcher 1.0.35 changes

- Hunt Damage and Behemoth Parts are now first on the launcher’s Client Mods page, with a Made by Void credit on both cards. This is a normal release and reaches the launcher auto-update feed.
- Restyled the HUD: a rounded translucent damage panel on the left with aligned coloured values and regular-weight labels, and a narrow single-column part list on the right.
- Replaced unsupported text-symbol dots with antialiased glowing image indicators. Parts have thin HP bars: green above half, orange at half or less, red for a confirmed break. Missing or fixed-part data stays gray.
- Uses the game’s RobotoCondensed font, removes the heavy text outline, and clips long part names inside the panel. Removed the part monitor headings, distance line and status-word badges.
- Home → Hunt Damage controls the optional team breakdown. Turn it off for the five-row reference view; existing preferences are preserved. Home → Behemoth Parts controls the part panel.

The HUD mods are optional Windows UE4SS features and remain disabled under Wine/Proton. The Windows and Linux launchers retain the existing Steam Deck startup fixes. Damage totals count combat events received by the client, not an authoritative server scoreboard.

Validation: launcher tests, Lua HUD regressions and release-package integrity checks. Native in-game appearance and the new texture-import path still need a real-hunt smoke test; native game access was unavailable in this session.
